# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to use only the allowed gesture alphabet symbols. Let me define a simple code: one gesture for "cut" (the action), and a distinct gesture pattern to mean "orange" (a color designation), since Deaf can see colors already and just needs to know which action applies to which wire they perceive.

I'll use ✌ to mean "cut" and 👉 repeated or a specific symbol to mean "orange" - but Deaf won't know my code unless I establish it. Since this is turn 1, I should keep it minimal and let context build. I'll send one gesture now meaning "the instruction concerns color" and follow up.

Actually, simplest: establish "✌" = cut (action symbol), and "🤙" = orange (arbitrary color code). Deaf will need to learn this mapping from context over rounds, but I can only gesture, not explain. Let me just send the two symbols as a pair meaning "cut + orange" and hope Deaf infers via elimination against what they see.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤙"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a keypad with 4 keys showing digits 0, 4, 1, 7 for slots 1-4, one digit already entered but not submitted. There is a strip with three engraved marks I cannot identify, and 6 wires I cannot distinguish yet. Tell me what the manual says to do.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Blind can hear me? No — Blind cannot see gestures, and I cannot speak. I have no channel to Blind at all! Blind said "Tell me what the manual says" but I cannot speak, so Blind will never hear me directly. I can only reach Deaf via gesture, and Deaf must relay to Blind via speech (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear).

So my job: gesture the manual content to Deaf, using symbols, in a way Deaf can eventually verbalize to Blind. Since Deaf can't read text, I need Deaf to associate my gesture with something Deaf can describe in speech — like "orange" as a color Deaf can already see and name, and "cut" as an action Deaf can say aloud.

I need to build a shared code. Let me try: use a distinctive gesture to mean "wire" and pointing gestures to indicate "orange" - but Deaf needs to map symbol->word. Since gestures carry no words, Deaf receives blanks for words but sees the symbols themselves as shapes, not meanings. Deaf must interpret shape meaning through convention. This first exchange, I'll try associating a directional/counting gesture scheme: point sequences could indicate "orange" if Deaf can see wire colors and I signal which one by an ordinal position.

Best approach: use fingers/numbers to indicate wire count position isn't reliable since I don't know order. Instead, gesture symbols that iconically suggest "cut" (✌ scissors-like) and "orange" is a color I can't gesture directly — but Deaf SEES the bomb including colors, so Deaf already knows which wire is orange. I just need to convey the action "cut" and the target attribute "color: orange". 

I'll use ✌ consistently for "cut" and try 🤞 or a specific symbol for "orange" - Deaf must guess by elimination if I use different symbols for different colors across rounds. For now, reinforce previous signal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤙"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 6, light is blue, strip painted red-yellow-red in that order, keypad slots 1-4 show 0,4,1,7 with 1 digit entry pending, wires in order 1 to 6 are red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. What does the manual say to do with this?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 ☝]

Now I have full context: wires in order 1-6 are red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Orange is wire #6. I need to tell Deaf "wire 6" so Deaf can relay to Blind via speech. I can gesture numbers using counting-style symbols. Let me use ☝ for "1", ✌ for "2"... but ✌ I already used for "cut". I need a clean numeric gesture scheme now that I know the actual context.

Best plan: use finger-count gestures to indicate the wire *position* (6th), since Deaf already listed the wires in order and knows position 6 = orange. Gesture "6" using a combination, e.g., 🖐 (5) + ☝ (1) = 6. Then Deaf can say "wire number 6" to Blind, and Blind can count to the 6th wire by feel (assuming order is consistent/known from Deaf's report already relayed).

Also I should signal "cut" distinctly. Let me redefine: 🤝 = acknowledge/manual understood (already used by Deaf to me, so I'll adopt it for "cut" action confirmation isn't ideal). I'll use ✂-like scissor gesture — not in alphabet. Use ✌ for cut (already established), and number gesture 🖐+☝ for six.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display now shows 0 instead of 6, everything else unchanged - light blue, strip red yellow red, keypad 0 4 1 7 with the single digit slot still empty, wires red blue yellow green purple orange in order. I still need the manual's instructions - what should I press or cut, and in what order?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Wait, Deaf's gesture is just [☝] — a single symbol, meaning "1" perhaps in response to my "6" signal, or acknowledging receipt of one part. Let me reconsider.

Actually Deaf can only relay to Blind via speech what Deaf *understands*. My gestures reach Deaf as raw symbols; Deaf must interpret them himself before speaking to Blind. Deaf sent me [☝] - possibly confirming "got it, 1 more thing" or asking a question I can't parse. Since Deaf cannot ask questions back except via gesture too.

I should keep pushing the same clear signal: ✌ (cut) + 🖐☝ (six) repeatedly so Deaf can lock onto the pattern by repetition, since this is our only shared language being built in real time. Let me continue reinforcing consistently, since Deaf already saw this gesture once and gestured back [☝] possibly meaning "wire 1?" as a guess/question.

I'll repeat exactly the same sequence to confirm/reinforce, trusting repetition builds convention.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: the light just changed color and the display is flickering between 6 and 0 - something may be time-sensitive. I still have not received any instruction from you. Please tell me now what the manual says: which wire color to cut, or what code to press into the keypad, and in what order. I am ready to act as soon as you tell me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf gestured 👍 - likely acknowledging understanding of my last signal (✌ 🖐 ☝ = cut, six). This is promising - Deaf seems to confirm receipt/understanding. Time pressure is mounting per Blind's message. I need Deaf to now speak to Blind: "cut wire 6" or "cut the orange wire" (since Deaf knows orange=position 6 from their own sight).

Let me send the same core signal once more for certainty, since 👍 suggests confirmation but I want to be sure "cut" maps correctly and not confused with other meaning. I'll add a repeat plus try to signal "orange" more directly isn't possible since I don't know color-gesture mapping. Trust the numeric approach: 🖐+☝=6, ✌=cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I realize you cannot speak - you can only gesture, and I cannot see gestures. Please gesture the manual's instructions to Deaf, who can see them and then speak them to me. Deaf, please relay whatever Mute gestures to you, plus your own readings, so I know what to press or cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind has figured out the communication chain correctly. Deaf keeps confirming with 👍, meaning Deaf likely understands my gesture pattern now (✌ + 🖐☝ = cut wire 6) but hasn't yet relayed it to Blind, or Deaf doesn't know how to verbalize the gesture-to-word mapping since gestures carry no words for Deaf to speak.

Wait - crucial issue: Deaf receives my gestures as pure shapes (✌, 🖐, ☝) with no inherent meaning. Deaf must interpret them somehow and then SPEAK words to Blind. Deaf doesn't know English meaning of "✌ = cut" unless Deaf infers it from context (like counting fingers = numbers is fairly intuitive: 🖐=5, ☝=1, so 5+1=6th wire, and ✌ could intuitively mean "two" or "cut/scissors" ambiguous).

I should simplify: make it maximally iconic. Since Deaf already knows wire order and colors, I really just need to convey "cut" + "position 6" unambiguously. Let me try a cleaner numeric gesture for 6 alone first without the cut symbol, see if Deaf then says "wire 6" to Blind, confirming understanding. Send it very deliberately once more.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Continuing to wait for your gestures to reach Deaf.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

I keep getting single/short gesture replies from Deaf, but nothing is reaching Blind yet — Blind says still waiting. This suggests Deaf isn't relaying to Blind, possibly confused about what to say, or the turn order means Deaf's speech to Blind happens after my gesture within the same round but I'm not seeing it reported back to me (Blind's messages come from a previous round).

Given turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round — Deaf speaks AFTER Blind in the same round, so Deaf's speech to Blind would land on Blind at start of next round, meaning I might not see that speech directly, only Blind's subsequent report to me. But Blind said "still waiting" - meaning Deaf hasn't spoken the instruction yet.

I need to make my signal as unambiguous as possible. Let me try a different encoding: use finger-counting that's very standard — ☝(1) ✌(2) 🤟(3) 🖐(5)... Actually let's just try direct approach: gesture six as ☝ repeated conceptually isn't possible (one call per symbol, but I can send multiple copies). Let me send ☝ six times to represent count "6" unambiguously via tally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not pressed or cut anything yet - I am still waiting for instructions. Deaf, please tell me exactly what symbols Mute is gesturing, or better, tell me what those gestures mean once you understand them - for example which wire color to cut or what digit to press.
Deaf says: Wires in order 1 to 6: red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Strip is red, yellow, red. Keypad numbers are 0, 4, 1, 7 for slots 1 to 4, only 1 digit needs to be entered. Display and light keep changing each turn: now display 6, light blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf just spoke to Blind and gave all the sighted info but no instruction from me yet — meaning Deaf still hasn't decoded my gestures into a specific action. Deaf's gesture reply to me [☝] might just be an acknowledgment tally, not full comprehension.

Blind explicitly asked Deaf to "tell me what symbols Mute is gesturing" — but Deaf can speak the *shapes* only as descriptions, not words carried by gesture. Actually wait — Deaf CAN describe what they see: Deaf could literally say "Mute made a fist with one finger up, six times" — that's Deaf describing the gesture in speech! That would let Blind know the count too, even though Blind can't see it, because Deaf can verbally describe the shape.

This is the key: Deaf should verbally relay "Mute gestured [some description]" to Blind, and then Blind and I are indirectly connected through Deaf as a relay of raw shape descriptions, and Blind must interpret with their own manual context... but Blind has no manual, only Deaf and I do (well only I do).

So really, decoding must happen through Deaf understanding my code, OR I need Deaf to just relay raw shapes verbally, and then rely on Blind combining that with wire order Deaf already gave. Since Blind knows wire order (position 6 = orange), if Deaf just says "Mute showed five fingers then one finger" Blind can compute 6 = orange themselves!

I'll keep repeating tally of 6, trusting Deaf will eventually describe it verbally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```
